whatChanged: NEW: The Information reported Nvidia has agreed to buy open-source AI model hub Hugging Face for $12.9bn -- what would be its largest acquisition ever, nearly double Mellanox -- though nothing is signed and the deal could still fall apart (nvda-huggingface-acquisition)

NEW: Advent International and Stripe abandoned their roughly $53bn, $60.50-a-share pursuit of PayPal after the board called the price insufficient and the two sides failed to close the gap; the stock fell 17% premarket (pypl-stripe-advent-takeover-bid)

NEW: AWS and NVIDIA expanded their partnership to deploy 2 million additional GPUs across AWS infrastructure in 2027-2028 -- tripling March's 1-million commitment -- alongside Vera CPU infrastructure, NVLink Fusion with custom high-bandwidth memory and a 100,000-GPU US government AI factory (amzn-nvidia-gpu-expansion)

themes.label: Public-to-private buyout offers on listed companies
themes.note: Sponsor-, sovereign-, cooperative- and strategic-led buyouts keep pulling listed names off public markets, but the failure count is now two in four days. Live and unresolved: Uber's BaFin-approved offer document opened a EUR41.50-a-share, ~EUR13bn cash tender for Delivery Hero running to 5 November with only a 50%-plus-one minimum (dher-uber-takeover-offer); Couche-Tard's PLN 32.00-a-share tender for Zabka is open to 25 September with 57% locked up by irrevocables (zab-couchetard-tender-offer); Curaleaf's hostile tender for Aurora Cannabis runs to 1 December against a special committee telling holders to sit tight (acb-curaleaf-takeover-bid); Silver Lake is in talks to take Workday private at a ~$43bn market value (wday-silverlake-takeover-talks); KKR has an unsolicited ~$9bn, $42.50-a-share approach on the table for UGI, with the board still evaluating (ugi-kkr-takeover-bid); WSP Global will file an offer memorandum with the Dutch AFM by 15 October to press a twice-rejected EUR51.50-a-share bid for Arcadis (arcad-wsp-takeover-bid); Abu Dhabi's L'IMAD is offering Dh6.25 a share for the ~24.6% of AD Ports it does not hold (adports-limad-takeover-bid); Deoleo has rival cash offers from Dcoop at EUR470m and Coricelli at EUR500m, the Italian bidder's ultimatum lapsing 31 August (ole-dcoop-takeover-bid, ole-coricelli-takeover-bid); JBS has proposed taking in the ~18% of Pilgrim's Pride it does not own at 2.086 JBS shares apiece, subject to a special committee and a majority-of-the-minority vote (ppc-jbs-minority-buyout); and InMode's special committee is free to rule on competing bids now the Haifa court has thrown out Steel Partners' injunction (inmd-steel-partners-buyout). Against that, two approaches have now died on price rather than on regulators: Trian shelved its Wendy's take-private and the stock handed back the whole premium (wen-trian-takeover-bid), and Advent and Stripe walked away from a $60.50-a-share, ~$53bn bid for PayPal after a 40% run in the shares squeezed the premium out of it (pypl-stripe-advent-takeover-bid). Already signed: Two Harbors' $12.00-a-share sale to CrossCountry Mortgage (two-crosscountry-acquisition), Francisco Partners' $650m for Weave (weav-francisco-partners-take-private), Thoma Bravo's $4bn+ for Accelerant (arx-thoma-bravo-take-private), Bernhard Capital's $43-a-share for Bowman (bwmn-bernhard-capital-takeover) and Safe Harbor's $53-a-share for MarineMax (hzo-safe-harbor-acquisition).

themes.label: AI data-center capacity and power build-out
themes.note: Capital keeps pouring into the physical layer of AI compute, and the commitments now run years ahead of the workloads: AWS has agreed to deploy 2 million additional Nvidia GPUs across its global footprint in 2027-2028, tripling the 1-million programme announced in March and adding Vera CPU infrastructure, custom-HBM NVLink Fusion and a 100,000-GPU US government AI factory (amzn-nvidia-gpu-expansion). The constraint underneath it has narrowed to energised power rather than plans for it, which is pulling in the regulated utilities themselves -- KKR's unsolicited ~$9bn approach for UGI's gas and electric utility, midstream and propane franchise is explicitly framed against data-center load growth (ugi-kkr-takeover-bid). The Ohio megaproject remains the clearest single example: Nvidia's backstop for OpenAI's PORTS-Pike campus is firm at up to $105bn of credit for the first 4.25GW, with an option covering a further 3.75GW (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop), and Nvidia has separately put $1.5bn of equity into developer SB Energy, which with SoftBank plans at least 10GW of new generation, a 9.2GW on-site gas plant costing ~$33bn and $4.2bn of Ohio grid investment (nvda-sbenergy-investment). Elsewhere Core Scientific paid ~$444m to take ~440MW of in-service, grid-connected Oklahoma capacity off a rival miner and push its Muskogee campus toward 1.5GW of AI colocation (corz-polaris-acquisition). How the build gets funded is the other half of the story: Nvidia has signed MOUs with six of the largest private-capital pools to mobilise over $500bn of third-party financing (nvda-compute-financing-platforms), Broadcom is sounding lenders for more than $60bn against a chip-leasing vehicle aimed at over 20GW of frontier-lab compute by 2028 (avgo-anthropic-chip-financing), and Intel is selling $15bn of new stock to fund fab capex (intc-equity-offering-2026). On the equipment side Madison Air is paying $5.4bn for ebm-papst's fans and motor systems partly for the data-center cooling opportunity (mair-ebmpapst-acquisition); at the silicon layer Marvell has locked Google into a multi-year custom-chip programme for the TPU ecosystem (mrvl-google-tpu-partnership), Sony and TSMC are putting JPY747bn into a Kumamoto image-sensor fab (sony-tsmc-image-sensor-jv), and Micron is committing $10bn over a decade to a Boise foundational-research hub (mu-research-labs-investment) while SK hynix returns a record KRW40trn of the HBM windfall to shareholders rather than adding a third leg of capacity (skhynix-buyback-cancellation-2026).

themes.label: Signed M&A deals hitting regulatory or legal roadblocks
themes.note: Deals investors thought were settled keep being resolved by judges, regulators and shareholder ballots, in both directions. Paramount Skydance has satisfied every regulatory condition in its Warner Bros. Discovery merger agreement, yet still cannot close until five days after a 12-day antitrust trial set for 2 March 2027 -- and the negotiated way out has broken down, with California AG Rob Bonta cancelling the settlement meeting and accusing Paramount of leaking and misrepresenting the previous session, leaving the $1.88bn bond demand and the $7m-a-day ticking fee from 30 September as the live pressure points (psky-wbd-acquisition). Western Union's Intermex deal cleared New York's DFS on 14 August only for California's DFPI to suspend its own approval extension the day before (imxi-westernunion-acquisition). Uber's newly opened tender for Delivery Hero shows how long the tail can be even on an agreed deal: merger-control and financial-regulatory clearances across a 99-country footprint push guided settlement out to the second half of 2027 (dher-uber-takeover-offer). Gates keep opening as well: Real's arrangement with RE/MAX cleared the Supreme Court of British Columbia and closed on 24 August, with Real REMAX Group trading on Nasdaq from the 25th (reax-remax-combination), Deutz's extraordinary general meeting backed the capital increase behind its EUR1.6bn FFG purchase with 99.7% in favour after an unconditional Bundeskartellamt clearance (dez-ffg-acquisition), Two Harbors received the last regulatory approval for its sale to CrossCountry Mortgage (two-crosscountry-acquisition), the Haifa court denied Steel Partners' injunction request in its entirety, releasing InMode's special committee to rule on the competing buyout bids (inmd-steel-partners-buyout), and California's PUC signed off on Charter-Cox as the final clearance needed, letting a $34.5bn merger close fifteen months after it was struck (chtr-cox-acquisition).

themes.label: Chipmakers funding or locking in the customers that buy their chips
themes.note: Vendor financing, equity and exclusivity remain the standard shape of frontier-AI deals, and the entanglement now runs in every direction at once. Nvidia's OpenAI backstop is a firm commitment of up to $105bn against the first 4.25GW of the Ohio campus (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop), and alongside it Nvidia has taken a $1.5bn equity stake in campus developer SB Energy that makes it the sole supplier of compute on the site it is financing (nvda-sbenergy-investment) -- the circularity critics object to, written into the cap table. It extends past financing into capability: Nvidia paid Poolside $6bn to license the 'Model Factory' training stack behind its Laguna models, put $1bn of equity into the startup and hired the 109 engineers who built it (nvda-poolside-model-factory-license), and it is now reported to have agreed $12.9bn for Hugging Face, the distribution point where developers pull the open-source models they then have to run on Nvidia silicon (nvda-huggingface-acquisition). The straightforward version of the trade still runs alongside all of it: AWS has committed to 2 million more Nvidia GPUs in 2027-2028 despite designing its own accelerators (amzn-nvidia-gpu-expansion). Broadcom has taken the financing trade further than anyone, seeking more than $60bn of debt for a vehicle that buys Broadcom's own custom chips and leases them to Anthropic and potentially OpenAI, with Broadcom guaranteeing part of the senior tranche (avgo-anthropic-chip-financing), while the syndicated version keeps scaling: the six-firm compute-financing platforms lend against Nvidia's own GPUs so buyers can afford them, moving the credit risk to Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR (nvda-compute-financing-platforms). Marvell has inverted the trade entirely, handing Google a warrant over up to $12.2bn of its own stock -- vesting only as Google buys chips -- so the customer ends up owning the supplier (mrvl-google-tpu-partnership).

themes.label: Financial firms buying platforms and product lines rather than building them
themes.note: Three live deals show listed financial companies concluding that the capabilities the market now pays for are quicker to buy than to build, and that what they are buying is a fee stream rather than plain assets. Victory Capital is paying about $7bn -- $4bn cash, $2bn in new shares and $575m of assumed notes -- for First Eagle Investments, taking combined assets to roughly $571bn and acquiring First Eagle's $41bn CLO and alternative-credit platform to serve as the enlarged group's alternatives arm (vctr-first-eagle-acquisition). Goldman Sachs is paying as much as $2.25bn in cash and equity for NEOS Investments and its 19 options-income ETFs with about $30bn of assets, buying a derivative-income and crypto-income ETF franchise it has no organic equivalent to (gs-neos-acquisition). At the small end, Velocity Financial is paying only $63m for KKR-backed Toorak's operating platform but taking on management of the ~$3bn loan portfolio sold alongside it, converting a balance-sheet lender into one that also earns fees on third-party capital (vel-toorak-platform-acquisition). In each case the target is a fee-rate-defensible platform rather than AUM, and the buyer faces compression in its own core business.
